references.text: Just before this verse, the crowd shouts, "Crucify him, crucify him!" ([ref:Luk 23:21|Luke 23:21]). Verse 23 describes how they continued to press with loud cries that he should be crucified.
The parallel account in [ref:Matt 27:22-23|Matthew 27:22-23] tells of the crowd's repeated calls for crucifixion and how they shouted even louder when Pilate asked what evil Jesus had done.
Mark's parallel account in [ref:Mark 15:13-14|Mark 15:13-14] depicts the crowd's persistent cries for crucifixion, which aligns with the pressure described in Luke 23:23.
In [ref:Joh 19:12-15|John 19:12-15], we see the same pressure from the crowd and the chief priests on Pilate, as they insist on crucifixion and threaten political consequences if he does not give in.

In [ref:Apg 2:23|Acts 2:23], Peter confirms that Jesus was handed over according to God's set purpose and plan, but that it happened by the hands of lawless men—a theological reflection on what occurred when the crowd's cries prevailed.

In [ref:Apg 3:13-14|Acts 3:13-14], Peter accuses the people of rejecting Jesus before Pilate's face, even though Pilate wanted to release him—this is exactly the situation in Luke 23:23 where the crowd's pressure overcame Pilate's reluctance.
Paul says in [ref:Apg 13:28|Acts 13:28] that although they found no basis for a death sentence, they asked Pilate to have him executed—an summary of the pressure described in Luke 23:23.

The prophecy in [ref:Jes 53:7-8|Isaiah 53:7-8] about the suffering servant who was taken away by oppression and judgment points forward to how Jesus was handed over for crucifixion through the overwhelming pressure of the crowd.
The immediate result of the crowd's pressure in verse 23 is seen in [ref:Luk 23:24-25|Luke 23:24-25], where Pilate gives in and pronounces the sentence they demanded.
